claim_1.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocyte frequencies increased at days 2 and 7 compared to baseline (day 0), with return toward baseline by day 28, and this induction did not differ between young and older adults.

sources.quote: We evaluated monocyte populations at each time point, and found induction of CD14+ CD16+ monocytes after influenza vaccination, particularly at days 2 and 7 after vaccination, with resolution toward baseline by day 28 (Figure 1); this induction of CD14+ CD16+ so-called inflammatory monocytes did not differ between young and older adults (Figure 1B).

claim_2.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-6 production in classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes was induced after vaccination in young adults compared to baseline (day 0), with highest levels at day 28, whereas older adults showed diminished induction compared to young adults.

sources.quote: We evaluated intracellular cytokine production in both classical CD14+ CD16− and inflammatory CD14+ CD16+ monocytes and found strong induction of intracellular IL-6 production relative to day 0 in both populations from young subjects at days 2 and 7, with highest levels found at day 28 (Figure 2A and 2B). In monocyte populations from older adults, this induction seemed dysregulated, with diminished expression seen at day 2 and weaker intracellular IL-6 levels in both populations compared with young subjects at days 7 and 28.

claim_3.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults classified by vaccine response before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with hemagglutination inhibition-defined vaccine response, with higher IL-6 in responders than nonresponders compared within age groups.

sources.quote: Notably, we found that the extent of intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with influenza vaccine response in both young and older adults at days 2 and 7 and in older adults at day 28 (Figure 3).

claim_4.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular TNF-α production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was higher in young adults than in older adults compared across age groups after vaccination.

sources.quote: For intracellular TNF-α production, higher levels were found in classical monocytes from young compared with those from older subjects at days 2, 7, and 28 and in inflammatory monocytes from young compared with older subjects at days 0, 2, and 7 (Figure 2).

claim_5.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults classified by vaccine response before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular TNF-α production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was associated with hemagglutination inhibition-defined vaccine response, with higher TNF-α in responders than nonresponders compared within age groups.

sources.quote: As with intracellular IL-6 production, the levels of intracellular TNF-α were also associated with vaccine response. In classical and inflammatory monocytes, intracellular TNF-α at day 2 was highest in young vaccine responders compared with young nonresponders (P < .001). At day 2, TNF-α production was also significantly higher in older responders than in older nonresponders in classical (P = .001) and inflammatory monocytes (P < .001). At day 7, intracellular TNF-α in both monocyte subsets was significantly higher in young responders than in young nonresponders (P < .001) or older nonresponders (P < .001) (Figure 3).

claim_6.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-10 levels in classical and inflammatory monocytes were markedly elevated in older adults compared to young adults at all time points.

sources.quote: Notably, the levels of intracellular IL-10 were markedly elevated in classical and inflammatory monocytes from older subjects at all time points, compared with those from young subjects.

claim_7.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-10 in classical monocytes increased progressively to highest levels at day 28 compared to baseline (day 0), whereas inflammatory monocyte IL-10 remained stable from days 0 to 2 before increasing at days 7 and 28.

sources.quote: In classical monocytes (Figure 2A), intracellular IL-10 increased progressively to highest levels at day 28 after vaccination, whereas in CD14+ CD16+ monocytes IL-10 levels seemed stable between days 0 and 2 before increasing at days 7 and 28 (Figure 2B).

claim_8.claim: flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young (n = 31) and older (n = 36) adults before vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-10 levels were associated with intracellular IL-6 levels in both classical and inflammatory monocytes compared across time points.

sources.quote: When these models included the levels of intracellular IL-10 in CD14+ CD16− monocytes at each time point, IL-10 levels were significantly (P = .004; type 3 test over all days) associated with the levels of intracellular IL-6 in CD14+ CD16− monocytes. A similar association between intracellular IL-10 and IL-6 was also found for inflammatory monocytes (P < .001; type 3 test over all days).

claim_9.claim: hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assays analysis of serum from young and older adults at baseline (day 0) and day 28 after influenza vaccination showed that vaccine response, defined by any 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any vaccine strain, was less frequent in older adults compared to young adults.

sources.quote: We subsequently classified subjects as influenza vaccine responders (defined as having any 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any of the 3 strains in the vaccine) or nonresponders (having no 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any vaccine strain); the proportions of responders and nonresponders differed between young and older adults (Supplementary Table 1).

claim_10.claim: Western blot analysis of PBMC lysates from a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed that phosphorylated STAT3 Y705 and STAT3 S727 levels were increased in older adults compared to young adults, while total STAT3 was unchanged.

sources.quote: In a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults from the original cohort, we found unchanged levels of total STAT3 protein but a significant baseline increase in STAT3 Y705 and S727 phosphorylation in older compared with young subjects (Figure 4B).

claim_11.claim: Western blot analysis of PBMC lysates from a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed that higher STAT3 Y705 or STAT3 S727 phosphorylation was inversely associated with hemagglutination inhibition-defined vaccine response compared to lower phosphorylation.

sources.quote: However, the baseline level of STAT3 Y705 or S727 phosphorylation showed significant inverse associations with influenza vaccine response in this subset (Figure 4B).

claim_12.claim: Western blot analysis of purified monocyte lysates from 6 young and 6 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed that phosphorylated STAT3 S727 levels were increased in older adults compared to young adults.

sources.quote: We subsequently studied monocytes purified via negative magnetic bead sorting in 12 newly recruited young and older adults, and we also found significantly increased levels of p-STAT3 S727 in monocytes from older adults, compared with those from young adults (Figure 5).

claim_13.claim: Western blot analysis of purified monocyte lysates from 6 young and 6 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed that total DUSP1 was slightly elevated, phosphorylated DUSP1 S296 was decreased, and phosphorylated DUSP1 S359 was substantially decreased in older adults compared to young adults.

sources.quote: We found a slight elevation in total DUSP1 (P = .03) in older versus young subjects that was associated with decreased phosphorylation at S296 (P = .005). However, we found a substantial decrease in S359 phosphorylated DUSP1 in monocytes from older subjects (P = .005), suggesting a basis for an age-associated increase in anti-inflammatory IL-10 production (Figure 5B).
